27.1.intro: You're the most important part of the business. How you sleep, plan and handle messages shapes every decision.

steps.say: Set a fixed bedtime and wake time for weekdays. Protect them.
steps.check: You sleep about the same hours every night.
steps.lost: Pick one bedtime. Stick to it this week.

steps.say: Each week, block your focus time in the calendar first. Fit meetings around it.
steps.check: Your calendar has protected focus blocks.
steps.lost: Block one 2-hour focus slot.

steps.say: Check messages at set times (like 9am, 1pm, 4pm). Turn off notifications you don't need.
steps.check: You're not pulled away all day.
steps.lost: Turn off one noisy notification.

steps.say: Give every meeting an agenda, one owner and a decision.
steps.check: Meetings end with a decision, often early.
steps.lost: Write 3 agenda points for your next meeting.

steps.say: Work in blocks of 25 or 45 minutes on one thing at a time.
steps.check: You finish deep tasks without switching.
steps.lost: Set a 25-minute timer. Do one thing.

steps.say: Work out what your hour is worth (like target yearly profit ÷ working hours). Example: $100,000 ÷ 2,000 hours = $50 an hour. Hand off work worth less.
steps.check: You have a list of tasks to hand off.
steps.lost: Write one task someone else could do.

steps.say: Say no to anything that doesn't help this cycle's priorities (Lesson 27.3).
steps.check: Your week matches your priorities.
steps.lost: Say no to one thing this week.

27.2.intro: A small daily and weekly rhythm keeps you on top of things in under an hour a week. The Helix routine is made for this.

steps.say: Every day, do the Helix routine (update yesterday, read your profit, do one task), plus one focus block on your top priority.
steps.check: Each day ends with your numbers in and one priority moved forward.
steps.lost: Update yesterday's numbers in Helix.

steps.say: Every Monday, spend 30 minutes planning the week: priorities, calendar and what to hand off.
steps.check: A Monday planning slot is in your calendar.
steps.lost: Add a 30-minute Monday slot.

steps.say: Every Friday, spend 15 minutes looking at what worked and what didn't.
steps.check: A Friday review slot is in your calendar.
steps.lost: Add a 15-minute Friday slot.

27.3.intro: One or two priorities with real time behind them beat ten half-done projects.

steps.say: Pick 1 or 2 priorities for the next six weeks.
steps.check: You have one or two written priorities.
steps.lost: Write your one big priority.

steps.say: Block 8 to 12 hours a week for them.
steps.check: The hours are in your calendar.
steps.lost: Block 2 hours a day, 4 days a week.

steps.say: Check progress every Friday. At the end of six weeks, review and pick the next priorities.
steps.check: You have a weekly check and a review date at week six.
steps.lost: Put a review in your calendar 6 weeks from now.

27.4.intro: Interruptions eat your time. Three quick questions decide what needs you now.

steps.say: When interrupted, ask: can it be explained in one sentence? Am I the right person? Does it need doing now?
steps.check: You can answer the three questions in seconds.
steps.lost: Ask: does this need me, right now?

steps.say: If any answer is no, say no, hand it to someone else, or schedule it for later.
steps.check: Only truly urgent things that are yours get your attention now.
steps.lost: Not urgent? Put it in your calendar for later.

27.5.intro: Handling a disagreement well builds trust. Keep it about the issue, not the person.

steps.say: Name the issue in one sentence. Then listen fully without interrupting.
steps.check: Both sides feel heard.
steps.lost: Say the problem in one sentence. Then listen.

steps.say: Separate facts from feelings. Agree on the result you both want.
steps.check: You have a shared goal.
steps.lost: Ask: what do we both want?

steps.say: Write down who will do what by when. Follow up to check it happened.
steps.check: There's a written agreement and a follow-up date.
steps.lost: Write one line: who, what, by when.

27.6.intro: There are five ways to pay for growth. Running the business as if a buyer will check it one day keeps every door open.

steps.say: List your funding options: profit put back in, longer supplier terms, inventory finance (loans for stock), revenue-based funding (pay back a share of sales), or selling shares (including crowdfunding).
steps.check: You know which options fit your stage.
steps.lost: Start with profit put back in.

steps.say: Keep clean numbers, written processes, and customer data you own.
steps.check: The business would pass a buyer's or lender's check.
steps.lost: Write down one process you do every week.
